ctx.x: Oh, yeah. Well, yeah. Well, you see, everything I do today is practically what he done for me. You see, because I've been having a few students coming to me from different schools around here. You tell them make C, they make the note of C. You see, make A, they make the note of A. Whoever is teaching them is going about the wrong way. Now, if you had a violin pupil, that would be right. Because a violin is a note instrument. But the banjo is a chord instrument. So, what you want to learn a man to do, you want to…

Here's something I want you to... Even if I have to interrupt your train of thought. There was one nice little thing you told me about once when you worked with Albert Glenny. He told you that pick out a good man to watch and then ask him questions and things like that. Do you remember? What was that he said to you once? Something about... Well, yeah, well... What was some advice he gave you?

Well, the older men had all kind of things. I mean, I don't so well remember that answer. But one thing he did tell me... We were talking about chords one night, you see. And he says, this is one thing about music. He said, D minor might be the right chord. It might be the right chord. He says, but if everybody in the band would make A7, we'll say. But they make it together, then it's the right chord. He says, but where it becomes a bad chord is if two is making D minor and the other fellow is making A7. Then you…
